links.comparator_used: Physician (clinician) ratings of all 118 query-response pairs across seven rubrics, used as the reference
links.outcome: Agreement between LLM judges and clinicians on clinical AI response grading
links.effect: High concordance on text-comparison rubrics (faithfulness, completeness) but weaker agreement on interpretive rubrics (reasoning, safety); no numeric values given in the abstract. Seven LLMs produced 17,346 ordinal and 8496 binary ratings versus 4130 physician ratings.
links.tradeoff: Weaker agreement on reasoning and safety dimensions; binary pass/fail evaluation exposed misalignments not apparent on ordinal scales.
links.quote: LLM judges showed high concordance on text-comparison rubrics such as faithfulness and completeness, but weaker agreement for interpretive dimensions like reasoning and safety.

links.outcome: Alignment of LLM judge ratings with physician ratings
links.effect: Multi-model panels did not systematically improve alignment beyond the best single model; no numbers given in the abstract.
links.quote: Repeated runs and multi-model panels did not systematically improve alignment beyond the best single model, while binary pass/fail evaluation exposed misalignments not apparent on ordinal scales.

design_hint: LLM-as-judge automated evaluation layer for clinical AI outputs
